name: Saint Martin de Porres
history: Son of a Spanish nobleman and a freed slave, Martin was a Dominican lay brother who served as barber, infirmarian and almoner. He cared for the sick, the poor, slaves and even animals, and was known for his humility and his gift of healing.
meditation: He called himself 'the mulatto dog'. Do one hidden act of service today that no one will thank you for.
life: Martin was born in Lima in 1579 to Juan de Porres, a Spanish nobleman, and Ana Velázquez, a freed black woman from Panama. His father was slow to acknowledge him, and the boy grew up poor. He was apprenticed to a barber-surgeon and learned to dress wounds and prepare remedies. At about fifteen he went to the Dominican priory of the Holy Rosary, where the law of the time allowed a man of his birth only to serve as a lay helper; in 1603 he was professed as a lay brother. He swept, shaved, nursed and begged alms, setting up care for orphans and the sick poor of the city. He was a friend of Saint Rose of Lima, and many stories tell of his healings and his gentleness with animals. He died in 1639 and was canonised by John XXIII in 1962.
prayerTo: Saint Martin de Porres, you were looked down on and answered with humble love, serving the sick, the poor and the forgotten of Lima. Pray for all who suffer because of their race or birth, and for me, that I may see Christ in each person I meet and serve Him gladly in the lowliest tasks. Amen.
penance: Do one humble, practical task today that others avoid, and give alms to a charity that cares for the sick poor.
